Question B-006-002-003.

Why the correct answer is right: Open-wire line uses two separate conductors kept a constant distance apart by insulating rods or spreaders. The large air spacing is part of its low-loss balanced-line behaviour.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Coaxial cable": Coaxial cable is built as nested conductors with dielectric between centre and shield, not as two wires on spreaders.
- sourceIndex 2: "Window line": Window line has its spacing maintained by a continuous or windowed plastic web, not by separate rods in open air.
- sourceIndex 3: "Twisted pair": Twisted pair conductors wrap around each other along the run, so it is not the spreader-supported open-wire construction.
